name: Eppeltone Engineers Ltd (EEPL)
tagline: Micro-cap electronic energy/smart-meter manufacturer riding India's national RDSS smart-metering rollout, with a large order book and stable ~18.5% ROCE - but this pass confirms a real, sourced cash-conversion problem (FY26 operating cash flow -Rs 18 Cr, free cash flow -Rs 38 Cr, working-capital days nearly tripling) consistent with the government/DISCOM-payment-cycle risk the original write-up flagged only qualitatively.
business_overview: Eppeltone designs, manufactures and supplies electronic energy meters, smart meters and power-conditioning devices, 100% B2B to state electricity boards, central PSUs, DISCOMs and turnkey contractors. It is riding India's RDSS (Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme, ~Rs 2.5 lakh Cr outlay) national smart-meter rollout; management expects the company could supply ~10-15% of total smart meters to be installed nationally. Eppeltone has applied for AMISP (Advanced Metering Infrastructure Service Provider) empanelment (expected 'in the next 1-2 months' as of a December 2025 update; current status not independently confirmed this pass), has won fresh Rs 41.46 Cr of IoT/metering-services orders and Rs 118.50 Cr of further order inflow in Q1 FY27, and carries an order book of roughly Rs 417-485 Cr (figures vary slightly by source/date) across Assam, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, with execution timelines on some contracts stretching to October 2027.

fundamentals_narrative: The core RDSS-driven growth story and capital-efficiency profile remain genuinely intact this pass: ROCE is stable at 18.5% (not declining), FY26 net profit grew +13%, and promoter holding actually rose slightly (61.67%->61.78%) - insiders are not exiting. However, this pass confirms a real cash-conversion problem the original write-up only flagged qualitatively ('execution and working-capital risk... are real'): FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 18 Cr and free cash flow -Rs 38 Cr despite growing reported profit, and working-capital days worsened sharply (from the ~79-86 day range to ~158-232 days across sources), with debtor days around 187. This is consistent with the well-known sector risk of slow government/DISCOM payment cycles, and Eppeltone's FY26 revenue growth of only +8.37% (Rs 124 Cr -> Rs 135 Cr) despite an order book roughly 3-4x that revenue suggests execution/conversion is genuinely gradual (some contracts run to October 2027), not imminent. This is a materially different, more cautious picture than a 'no red flags found' light pass would suggest, though - importantly - it is a liquidity/working-capital risk rather than a profitability collapse (unlike some other names in this pass's batch, PAT and ROCE here have NOT deteriorated).

verdict_headline: Genuine RDSS-driven smart-meter growth story with stable ROCE, growing PAT and rising promoter holding - but this pass confirms a real cash-conversion problem (FY26 OCF -Rs 18 Cr, FCF -Rs 38 Cr, working-capital days nearly tripling) consistent with known government-payment-cycle risk. Conviction downgraded Medium -> Low-Medium pending evidence the cash-flow trend is stabilising; four_box and thesis_fit retained given the underlying profitability hasn't deteriorated.
verdict_reasoning: Deep-dive pass 1 confirms the working-capital/execution risk the original pass flagged only qualitatively is real and material: FY26 operating cash flow -Rs 18 Cr and free cash flow -Rs 38 Cr despite +13% PAT growth, with working-capital days worsening sharply.

Unlike other names in this batch, the core profitability signal here is NOT deteriorating - ROCE is stable (18.5%), PAT is growing (+13% FY26), and promoter holding is rising slightly, not falling. This keeps the finding at a liquidity/working-capital-risk level rather than a profit-quality collapse.

four_box unchanged at 3.5 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation yes - still ~14x P/E is not demanding for the ROCE/order-book profile); thesis_fit retained at 10x-in-2-3-years given the underlying growth/return story remains intact even with the cash-flow caveat.

No red-flag-tier trigger found (no auditor resignation, no promoter pledge, no SEBI/fraud action); conviction downgraded Medium -> Low-Medium given the newly confirmed, material cash-conversion problem, pending evidence of stabilisation in the next 1-2 quarters.
revisit_after_30d set true - the AMISP empanelment resolution and the next quarter's cash-flow/working-capital trend are the key things to check next pass.
